extracted.intended_audience: theatregoers, playwrights/impresarios, critics, and polite literate readers (early-18th-century London)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance and critical criteria for staging operas, writing about the stage, and composing essays intended for polite society; covers scenic consistency, practical production cautions, literary style, and the appropriate tone for writings addressed to women and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow lavish decorations only to gratify the senses
rubrics_metrics.description: An Opera may be allowed to be extravagantly lavish in its Decorations, as its only Design is to gratify the Senses, and keep up an indolent Attention in the Audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lavishness is permissible because the design is sensory gratification, but it must not cross into childishness or absurdity; decoration should sustain, not undermine, the audience's suspended belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid childish and absurd scenes/machines
rubrics_metrics.description: Common Sense however requires that there should be nothing in the Scenes and Machines which may appear Childish and Absurd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern examples: Nicolini exposed to a Tempest in Robes of Ermin, painted dragons spitting wild-fire, enchanted chariots drawn by Flanders mares, and real cascades in artificial landscapes. Such absurdities invite ridicule rather than admiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mix shadows and realities in the same piece
rubrics_metrics.description: A little Skill in Criticism would inform us that Shadows and Realities ought not to be mix'd together in the same Piece; and that Scenes, which are designed as the Representations of Nature, should be filled with Resemblances, and not with the Things themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When representing a wide champaign country, avoid both painted scenes and real animals simultaneously (e.g., drawing the country on the scenes and crowding the stage with sheep and oxen); joining real and painted elements creates inconsistency and ruins illusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage realism must be consistent and practical
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenes designed as representations of nature should be filled with resemblances, and not with the Things themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical cautions: use of live animals (sparrows, mice) can lead to uncontrolled incursions into inappropriate scenes (e.g., birds flying into a lady's bed-chamber or perching on a king's throne) and hazards to audience heads; consider controllability and consequences before employing real creatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid implausible or inconsistent character/conceptual combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is very much puzzled to find how an Amazon should be versed in the Black Art, or how a [good] Christian should deal with the Devil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain internal plausibility of characters and plot devices; juxtaposing incongruous character types or ideological positions (e.g., Christian conjuror) undermines credibility and invites criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be skeptical of grandiose claims in prefaces and publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: He afterwards proceeds to call Minheer Hendel, the Orpheus of our Age, and to acquaint us ... that he Composed this Opera in a Fortnight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be persuaded by hyperbolic promotional language (calling composers 'Orpheus', boasting brief composition times); judge the work itself rather than inflated preface claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer substantive poetic worth to tinsel and ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: One Verse in Virgil is worth all the Clincant or Tinsel of Tasso.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique floral or tedious circumlocution and poor conceits; value concise, substantial poetic expression over florid but vacuous ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production should consider seasonality and audience comfort
rubrics_metrics.description: There was actually a Project of bringing the New River into the House, to be employed in Jetteaus and Water-works... when it is thought the Coolness that proceeds from Fountains and Cascades will be more acceptable and refreshing to People of Quality [in summer].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match ambitious stage effects to appropriate seasons and audience expectations; extravagant mechanical or water effects may be more suitable for summer and must be weighed against comfort and safety (insuring the house recommended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not introduce impossible large-scale stage spectacles lightly
rubrics_metrics.description: It had been proposed to break down a part of the Wall, and to surprize the Audience with a Party of an hundred Horse, and that there was actually a Project of bringing the New River into the House.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider logistical realism: proposals for cavalry, huge waterworks, or massive live spectacles may be impractical and dangerous; producers should avoid staging effects they cannot control safely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a refined, elevating tone when writing for women
rubrics_metrics.description: When it is a Woman's Day, in my Works, I shall endeavour at a Stile and Air suitable to their Understanding... I shall not lower but exalt the Subjects I treat upon. Discourse for their Entertainment, is not to be debased but refined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When addressing female readers, adopt a style that both suits their understanding and seeks to elevate subjects rather than debase them; aim for 'tea-table talk' that is pleasing and morally refined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance discretion with public moral critique regarding love
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever Skill I may have in Speculation, I shall never betray what the Eyes of Lovers say to each other in my Presence. At the same Time I shall not think myself obliged by this Promise, to conceal any false Protestations which I observe made by Glances in publick Assemblies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect private intimacies (do not betray lovers' signals), but feel free to expose public falsehoods and insincere displays observed in assemblies; writings should promote sincerity in love and condemn false protestations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat falsehood in love as a serious moral failing
rubrics_metrics.description: Falsehood in Love shall hereafter bear a blacker Aspect than Infidelity in Friendship or Villany in Business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign significant moral weight to deceit in romantic matters and examine breaches against love severely; social commentary should hold lovers to high standards of sincerity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value honesty and virtue above mere wit and fashionable polish
rubrics_metrics.description: There is hardly that Person to be found, who is not more concerned for the Reputation of Wit and Sense, than Honesty and Virtue... The Affectation of being gay and in fashion has very near eaten up our good Sense and our Religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and society should prize the application of wit toward public good and integrity rather than admiring wit or polish for their own sakes; moderation, reason, and virtue should guide judgments of character and works.

rubrics_metrics.name: When criticizing social practices, regard superstition as harmful
rubrics_metrics.description: We turn the most indifferent Circumstances into Misfortunes... A Rusty Nail, or a Crooked Pin, shoot up into Prodigies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose and mock superstitious fears that multiply imaginary evils; public discourse should employ philosophical reasoning to retrench such groundless terrors rather than amplify them.
